questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet. Calculators may be used.

A trader sends his staff on a training course costing $100 per person. 10 staff attended in April and 4 in May. Half the total cost had to be paid at the start of April and the balance at the end of May. Which entry for training was made in the statement of financial position on 30 April?
A business paid $10000 for motor expenses in the year. The opening prepayment was $1500 and the closing accrual was $2000. What was the charge for motor expenses for the year?
An item of revenue expenditure is wrongly treated as capital expenditure. What is the effect of this error? non-current profit for the assets year
A trader prepares a disposal account. On which sides do the cost of the asset and sale proceeds appear? cost of the asset sale proceeds

A trial balance at 30 June, before making end of year adjustments, showed the following. debit credit $ $ trade receivables 35600 – provision for doubtful debts – 1160 At 30 June, it was decided to write off a bad debt of $1600 and to make a provision for doubtful debts equal to 2% of trade receivables. What was the total decrease in the profit for the year ended 30 June arising from the bad and doubtful debts?

Land and buildings are shown in the books of account at a cost price of $200000 with accumulated depreciation of $40000. The property is revalued at $340000. Which entries record this transaction? debit credit account $ $

options.B: land and buildings 140000 provision for depreciation 40000 income statement 180000
options.D: land and buildings 140000 provision for depreciation 40000 revaluation reserve 180000

questions.questionText: At 1 January 2014 a business had prepaid rent of $700. In July it paid an invoice for $9300 and on 31 December it transferred an expense of $9000 to the income statement. Which value appeared in the statement of financial position at 31 December 2014?
Which cost should be treated as revenue expenditure?

options.A: installing a new sound system in a car
options.B: purchase of a trailer for a car
options.C: replacing a damaged engine of a car
options.D: replacing an old car with a new one

questions.questionText: A sales return of $400 has been credited to the customer’s account as $40.

Rachel’s trial balance did not agree and she placed the difference in a suspense account. The following shows how four errors have been corrected using the suspense account. suspense account $ $ difference in trial balance 200 discount received 310 discount allowed 160 sundry expenses 390 cash 340 700 700 The profit for the year before the errors were corrected was $35400. What is the correct profit for the year?

questions.questionText: Which item may appear in the manufacturing account of a business?
Inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value. What is net realisable value?

options.C: selling price less further cost to completion

questions.questionText: A trader runs a manufacturing business. Which department should it close?

options.A: department 1 where contribution exceeds fixed costs
options.B: department 2 where contribution is less than fixed costs
options.C: department 3 where revenue exceeds marginal costs
options.D: department 4 where revenue is less than marginal costs

questions.questionText: A club provides the following information. $ opening subscriptions in advance 1200 subscriptions received during the year 25000 closing subscriptions in arrears 1500 How much are subscriptions for the year in the income and expenditure account?
Which items increase when a company issues new shares?
When is working capital most likely to increase?

options.A: when the business increases its selling prices
options.B: when the credit period allowed to customers is reduced
options.C: when the credit period taken from suppliers is increased
options.D: when the value of inventory decreases

questions.questionText: John failed to write off a bad debt of $8000. What was the effect of this omission?

options.A: His trade payables turnover (in days) was overstated.
options.B: His trade payables turnover (in days) was understated.
options.C: His trade receivables turnover (in days) was overstated.
options.D: His trade receivables turnover (in days) was understated.

questions.questionText: A customer places an order for 20000 bricks. Which costing method will the supplier use to price the order?
Which item is classed as a direct cost?

A business sells its product for $50 a unit and has variable costs of $30 per unit. Its fixed costs for this year were $200000. Next year, fixed costs are expected to be $260000. How many more units will have to be sold next year to make the same profit as this year?

A manufacturer produces 100000 tins of paint with a total direct materials cost of $300000. Direct labour is 2000 hours at a cost of $400000, and overheads are absorbed at the rate of $100 per direct labour hour. What is the cost of a tin of paint?

A business provides the following information. number of total overheads month machine hours $ August 72000 842000 September 84000 938000 The variable overhead rate per machine hour was $8. What was the monthly fixed cost?

A business produces a single product. number of units opening inventory 5000 production 15000 closing inventory 2000 The variable production cost per unit is $10 and the fixed production cost is $60000. The sales revenue is $360000. Profit is $108000 based on full absorption costing. What is the profit based on marginal costing?
